introduction: Bram the Drake has come down to the trough to be fair to you. He genuinely thinks that is what he is doing.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Attacking the animal instead of the argument. How long Rue has been on the farm is not evidence about the pond.
Treating a crowd as a reason. Forty-one animals agreeing is not forty-one animals having checked.

sentences.text: You'll want to hear this before Sunday: the whole Flock has already agreed the pond should be ours.

logicalFallacies.explanation: The Flock agreeing is offered as the reason the pond should be theirs. Agreement is not a reason — it is just a number of animals.

sentences.text: Forty-one of us. You can't have forty-one animals be wrong about water.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Forty-one animals absolutely can be wrong about water, especially if none of them has been to the outflow.

sentences.text: Duchess puts the motion to Tobias at the Public Farm.
And frankly, the only one making a fuss is the donkey, and nobody knew his name a month ago.

logicalFallacies.explanation: How recently the farm learned Rue's name is a fact about Rue, not about the pond. The objection is dismissed without ever being answered.

sentences.text: Everyone I've asked says the hooves are the problem.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Everyone Bram asked is the Flock, and the Flock already agreed. Asking a crowd that shares a view is not evidence.

sentences.text: The grate at the outflow's bent, but that's been bent for ages.
